Album / Artist: Different When It's Silent / Tricky

Label: False Idols

Release Date: July 17, 2026

Review Date: 10/4/2026

Reviewer: DJ Stace

General Comments / Reviews:

Tricky's best in years. Dark, guitar-heavy trip-hop, with Mitch Sanders' ghostly falsetto doing a lot of the heavy lifting. - DJ Stace

Release Notes:

Bristol producer Adrian Thaws' 15th studio album and first full-length under his own name in six years, on his own False Idols label.

Bristol singer Mitch Sanders, 22, sings top lines on 12 of 14 tracks in a high falsetto; guests also include Marta Złakowska, Radana and Run Red Rambo.

Reviewers note distorted guitars, hypnotic basslines and electronic textures, with Tricky's low growl underneath.

released July 17, 2026

FCCs: 6,10

RIYL: Massive Attack, Portishead, Martina Topley-Bird

Play: All but FCCs, Favs Rated with up to *****

Tracklist:

1. **** I Still See Me There 03:39 - Slow, plodding, whispering, sinister and Trypnotic. Falsetto vocals float over Tricky’s growling whispers. Tricky is back. Sourced: Called too close to a blunted Maxinquaye outtake (Metacritic excerpt); Featuring Mitch Sanders (Bandcamp credits).
2. ** I'm Yours 02:36 - Medium paced bass and snare dominant rhythm line. Feat. Mitch Sanders falsetto; Interludes of Walls of sound applied to EDM. Sourced: Tricky and Mitch Sanders build great walls of electric sound (Metacritic excerpt).
3. *** Be Still In The Pain 03:22 - Upbeat by Tricky standard. Feat. Mitch Sanders and Run Red Rambo great falsetto duet juxtaposition. Abrupt ending. Sourced: Featuring Mitch Sanders and Run Red Rambo (Bandcamp credits).
4. *** I Tried 02:16 - Soft guitar intro, gives way to buzzing plodding marching rhythm and metallic guitar accompaniment with bass and vocal interludes. Sourced: Featuring Mitch Sanders (Bandcamp credits).
5. So Cold 02:39 - Medium to uptempo ticking and buzzing tapper. “Bright,” for Tricky. Sourced: Featuring Mitch Sanders (Bandcamp credits).
6. Paris Maybe 02:53 - Pretty straightforward guitar, bass and drums rock ballad? Would be at home in the 90’s segued to Divinyl. Not bad, but seems sonically isolated from the rest of the album. FCC fuck x1, shit x1. Sourced: Abrasive vocals, too short for the verses to land (Northern Transmissions).
7. *** Cannon Fodder 02:48 - Organ & heartbeat intro. Breathy falsetto is right up front. Transitions to some very fuzzy, desert rock guitar solo, then back to breathy whispers and organ to the end. Sourced: Cathartic dirge: quivering organ and flickering pulse interrupted by noisy guitar (AllMusic).
8. ***** Because I Don't Know 04:34 - Sinister, falsetto, trancy, repetitive, infectious groove. This is the hit on the record. Wall of sound drops with soaring falsetto crescendos are great. Can’t play it enough. Sourced: Read as a plea for understanding and empathy (AllMusic).
9. ** Marinade 03:20 - String intro, gives way to “Velvet Undergroundish” bass riff and spoken lyrics. Kinda cool. Would segue well with Kae Tempest. Abrupt ending. Sourced: Tricky experimenting with instrumental textures (Northern Transmissions).
10. Radana 03:10 - Middle Eastern flavor to the underlying music. Lyrics go hard. Would segue well with DAM. Feat. RMR & Radana. FCC fuck x3, piss x1, bitch x2. Sourced: Guest rapper Radana brings the genre's raw power to a nod to trip-hop's past (AllMusic).
11. *** Piano 02:43 - Piano and vocals with light atmospherics transition to strings and operatic chorale accompaniment. Lovely. Another abrupt ending. Sourced: Only Mitch's vocals, plus piano, violins and a vocal choir (AllMusic).
12. **** Frontier Town 01:40 - Killer stomp, cap and cal.,Clearly inspired by field songs. If Alan Lomax recorded EDM, this would be on his radar. Segue with Delta blues or field recordings from Parnman Farm. short. Sourced: Grouped with Marinade as instrumental-texture experiments (Northern Transmissions).
13. **** Hengrove Blues 02:57 - Soft acoustic strummer about a Bristol neighborhood. Lovely falsetto vocals with Tricky’s low growl underneath. Sourced: Acoustic arrangement that leans almost into folk (AllMusic).
14. *** Out of Place 02:38 - Quiet operatic opening vocals give way to a fast-paced staccato growling rocker with Tricky and Marta Złakowska’s vocals full forward. . Lead single (April 2026, announced the album). Sourced: First single, featuring Marta Zlakowska. Video directed by Steve Gullick (Joy of Violent Movement); Punkish rush that fades out as abruptly as it begins (AllMusic).
